name: Early, on the ebb
say: Low water. The ebb is pouring out over the bar at two and a half knots into a rising north-westerly: a fast ride out and a lumpy one. This is the bar to respect

name: Late morning
say: The ebb is easing and the breeze is filling in: 12 knots at the Gate, 10 to 15 from the north-west outside. The time to leave for anywhere

name: Early afternoon
say: The flood has made and the sea breeze is in: 18 knots at the Gate with gusts over 20, a steady 15 from the north-west offshore

name: Late afternoon
say: Twenty knots through the Gate, gusting 26, on the last of the flood. Coming home, it is a run in under the bridge with the sun behind you

name: After dark
say: The lights are lit and the night ebb is running over the bar, 14 knots of westerly still blowing over it. Ships in the lanes are a row of lights

name: Saturday at first light
say: A grey dawn, 13 knots of westerly and a fair tide just turning: the whole day ahead for the islands or the coast
